scenes.tts: Why can't a young songbird catch up on a song it never heard?
scenes.visual: Title card: One Input, Many Ages. A small sparrow on a branch beside a question mark.
scenes.narration: Why can't a young songbird catch up on a song it never heard?

scenes.tts: A male white-crowned sparrow raised without adult song still sings. But its song is simple and abnormal.
scenes.visual: Two spectrograms side by side: a wild white-crowned sparrow song with rich detailed structure, and an isolate's simpler song. Labels: wild song; raised without adult song.
scenes.narration: A male white-crowned sparrow raised without adult song still sings. But its song is simple and abnormal.

scenes.tts: The right song played later does little to fix it. Yet the bird is not deaf, and its voice works.
scenes.visual: A speaker plays song to an adult bird; its spectrogram stays simple. Check marks beside an ear and the syrinx: hearing works, vocal organ works.
scenes.narration: The right song played later does little to fix it. Yet the bird is not deaf, and its voice works.

scenes.tts: It missed an experience at the right age.
scenes.visual: A timeline of the bird's life with an early stretch highlighted and left empty.
scenes.narration: It missed an experience at the right age.

scenes.tts: Peter Marler asked when it must come. He raised young sparrows in sound-isolated chambers.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Peter Marler, 1960s and 1970s. A row of sound-isolated chambers, each holding one young sparrow.
scenes.narration: Peter Marler asked when it must come. He raised young sparrows in sound-isolated chambers.

scenes.tts: He played them recorded song at chosen ages. Then he waited, and recorded what they sang as adults.
scenes.visual: A timeline in days after hatching. Tape icons drop onto it at an early age, at a later age, and not at all for a third bird. An arrow runs forward to adulthood.
scenes.narration: He played them recorded song at chosen ages. Then he waited, and recorded what they sang as adults.

scenes.tts: Predict. Some birds heard the tape early, some later, some never. Which ones sing a good copy?
scenes.visual: Three birds with their tutoring histories: early tape, later tape, no tape. Each has an empty adult spectrogram and a question mark.
scenes.narration: Predict. Some birds heard the tape early, some later, some never. Which ones sing a good copy?

scenes.tts: Birds that heard song early sang good copies, though months passed before they first sang.
scenes.visual: The early-tape bird's adult spectrogram fills in and matches the tutor song. On screen: months between hearing and singing.
scenes.narration: Birds that heard song early sang good copies, though months passed before they first sang.

scenes.tts: Tapes played to older birds had little effect. Birds that heard no adult song sang simple, abnormal songs.
scenes.visual: The later-tape bird's spectrogram stays poor; the no-tape bird's is simple. Labels: little effect; abnormal.
scenes.narration: Tapes played to older birds had little effect. Birds that heard no adult song sang simple, abnormal songs.

scenes.tts: The same tape, at different ages, left very different marks.
scenes.visual: The three adult spectrograms in a row under one tape icon, labelled by age at tutoring.
scenes.narration: The same tape, at different ages, left very different marks.

scenes.tts: Marler's result splits learning into two phases. First, a sensory phase: the bird listens and memorizes.
scenes.visual: Timeline with two bands. Band 1 labelled sensory phase: listen and memorize. An ear icon.
scenes.narration: Marler's result splits learning into two phases. First, a sensory phase: the bird listens and memorizes.

scenes.tts: Then a sensorimotor phase: it practices, shaping rambling sounds until they match the memory.
scenes.visual: Band 2 labelled sensorimotor phase: practice and match. Rambling waveforms tighten toward a target.
scenes.narration: Then a sensorimotor phase: it practices, shaping rambling sounds until they match the memory.

scenes.tts: What does practice need? Masakazu Konishi deafened young sparrows after they heard a tutor, but before they practiced.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Masakazu Konishi. A timeline: hears tutor, then deafened, then the practice phase begins.
scenes.narration: What does practice need? Masakazu Konishi deafened young sparrows after they heard a tutor, but before they practiced.

scenes.tts: Their songs were extremely abnormal, no better than those of birds deafened before ever hearing a tutor.
scenes.visual: Two adult spectrograms, both disordered and alike. Labels: heard tutor, then deafened; deafened before ever hearing a tutor.
scenes.narration: Their songs were extremely abnormal, no better than those of birds deafened before ever hearing a tutor.

scenes.tts: So a bird must hear itself, to match its practice to a stored memory: a template.
scenes.visual: A stored waveform labelled template. The bird's practice waveform converges on it step by step. A deafened bird's practice wanders and never converges.
scenes.narration: So a bird must hear itself, to match its practice to a stored memory: a template.

scenes.tts: That defines a window. Plot what lasts against the age at which the input was given.
scenes.visual: The axes labelled: copy of tutor song (lasting outcome) against age at tutoring. Two ghost curves begin to draw.
scenes.narration: That defines a window. Plot what lasts against the age at which the input was given.

scenes.tts: This course calls a window that ends abruptly a critical period, like a door.
scenes.visual: A step curve: high, then an abrupt drop. A door icon swings shut at the step. Label: critical period (this course's usage).
scenes.narration: This course calls a window that ends abruptly a critical period, like a door.

scenes.tts: A window that fades gradually it calls a sensitive period, like a tide. Researchers also use these terms in other ways.
scenes.visual: A smooth ramp curve: high early, then a gradual decline. A tide icon going out. Label: sensitive period (this course's usage). Note on screen: schematic, not data; other authors use the terms differently.
scenes.narration: A window that fades gradually it calls a sensitive period, like a tide. Researchers also use these terms in other ways.

scenes.tts: The clearest human case here, second-language grammar, is a tide in the outcome. Telling them apart takes the whole curve.
scenes.visual: Both curves overlaid; a single dot labelled one summary number sits where both curves could pass through it.
scenes.narration: The clearest human case here, second-language grammar, is a tide in the outcome. Telling them apart takes the whole curve.

scenes.tts: So here is the one idea to carry. Same input, different ages: measure what lasts.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card: Same input, different ages: measure what lasts.
scenes.narration: So here is the one idea to carry. Same input, different ages: measure what lasts.

scenes.tts: In zebra finches, the expected input itself seems to help end the window.
scenes.visual: The card adds two lines: in most of these cases, fades gradually; in zebra finches, the expected input helps end it.
scenes.narration: In zebra finches, the expected input itself seems to help end the window.

scenes.tts: A window is a range of ages when the same experience leaves an unusually strong, lasting mark.
scenes.visual: Closing card: A window: ages when the same experience leaves an unusually strong lasting mark, compared with other ages.
scenes.narration: A window is a range of ages when the same experience leaves an unusually strong, lasting mark.
